change.title: Consolidate professional video and Mono Pro 17 definitions from 8 June 1982
change.reason: Set the Autodesk professional handover to 1982-06-08 with day precision and remove the approximate wording. For both devices, retain exactly the complete technical definition, BOM and assembly requirements from version 2 as the sole version 1, beginning at that handover and ending at the simulation horizon. The author intends a single specification rather than a later hardware revision. Update all eight version-2 pins in five products in the same atomic proposal so no dependent BOM becomes invalid; product contents and launch dates remain unchanged. Preserve all qualification caveats in the retained definitions.

before.title: Professional 800x600 hardware becomes available to Autodesk
before.description: Around June, deliver the 128 KiB professional video card and Logix Mono Pro 17 to Autodesk development and QA, with the 64 KiB colour card, Color Pro 14 and mouse. Four simultaneous shades are selected from 16 grayscale levels. Start full dual-display, acceleration and mouse integration; freeze qualified timing, bus and memory contracts.

inputs.description: The agreed dual-display and mouse interface requirements define the professional integration work that starts with this handover.

outcomes.description: The professional card, Mono Pro 17, colour card/display and mouse become available to the Autodesk development and QA team for integration. This records delivery to the team, not invention or general retail release of those devices.

before.name: Logix Artemis Professional 128 KiB video card
before.description: Logix Artemis Professional 128 KiB video card

specification.slot: One general 32-bit expansion slot; coexists with the dedicated primary video card
specification.memory_policy: 11072 bytes remain for bounded scratch/cursor work; allocations must be accounted for. No second framebuffer or inherited five-sprite subsystem is promised.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

specification.slot: One general 32-bit expansion slot; coexists with the dedicated primary video card
specification.mode_policy: Retain the June 64 KiB card text/bitmap modes and five-sprite behaviour, with explicit per-mode allocation and monitor capability checks. The 640x400x2 and 640x200x4 modes are inherited; 800x600x2 is the professional drawing mode.

palette_list.encoding: Byte 0: unsigned scanline delta; byte 1: palette-register index in high nibble, R in low nibble; byte 2: G in high nibble, B in low nibble. RGB components are 4 bits each.
palette_list.execution: Deltas accumulate from output active-line zero. Delta zero applies another write at the same boundary. Execute in preceding horizontal blank and latch before the target active line. Explicit count 0..512; a 10-bit count register avoids ambiguous terminators.
palette_list.long_gaps: Split gaps over 255 lines using harmless writes of an unchanged palette entry. These consume list entries.
palette_list.frame_state: Restore initial palette and reset list position at vertical blank. Software swaps or edits the active list only in a defined safe interval.
palette_list.write_limit: Design target at most four palette writes per output-line boundary, inherited from the June list budget; qualify transfer/settling against the faster raster before guaranteeing it. Reject over-budget lists rather than silently changing their timing.
palette_list.cad_policy: Static grayscale palette is the CAD default. Per-line palette changes are optional; 512 writes do not mean 512 distinct lines or 16 independent pixel shades in a 2bpp mode.

acceleration: Overlap-safe rectangle copies with stride and clipping
Rectangle fills and masked Boolean raster operations
Optional lookup-table antialiased lines with four output shades at 800x600
specification.redraw: Retain vector geometry; regenerate dirty regions and exposed pan strips. XOR may serve temporary simple cursors, not deletion of overlapping antialiased geometry. No 800x600 2bpp full-frame double buffering.
specification.sprites: Five legacy sprites use separate 1 KiB SRAM (two AION 2114 chips), outside the 128 KiB framebuffer/list allocation. Extend coordinate/addressing and line-budget validation to the 800x600 raster; no automatic sixth pointer sprite.
specification.monitor_modes: Mono Pro 17 uses a qualified fixed 800x600 raster. Older modes can be centered without scaling; the card reports presentation geometry and logical/output coordinate mapping. Older full-screen timings are enabled only for a monitor profile explicitly supporting them. No automatic multisync claim.
specification.host_integration: One general 32-bit Artemis slot for the additional professional card; the primary 64 KiB colour card keeps the dedicated video slot. Independent display handles, palettes, clocks, DMA/address resources and input focus.

composition_definition.element_type: Separate 1 KiB sprite SRAM; not charged against 128 KiB display RAM

specification.scan: 800x600 progressive; 60 Hz production target subject to OEM qualification
specification.oem_basis: Period 17-inch monochrome OEM assembly, with Ball HD17H family as a candidate rather than a confirmed supplier. Published Ball HD 26-36 kHz range does not meet the 37.5 kHz target without modification. Its digital video amplifier is not evidence of grayscale support.
specification.qualification: Qualify revised deflection, analog grayscale amplifier and high-speed digital link; no stock-monitor plug compatibility or final OEM contract assumed.

assembly_requirements.description: Engineering baseline; electrical qualification, routing and supplier quotes pending.

specification.scan: 800x600 progressive; 60 Hz production target subject to OEM qualification
specification.oem_basis: Period 17-inch monochrome OEM assembly, with Ball HD17H family as a candidate rather than a confirmed supplier. Published Ball HD 26-36 kHz range does not meet the 37.5 kHz target without modification. Its digital video amplifier is not evidence of grayscale support.
specification.qualification: Ball documents 26-36 kHz horizontal and 40-80 Hz vertical; optional linear amplifier is 35 MHz typical. 60 Hz at the selected totals needs a qualified OEM deflection revision. Pixel clock is not analog bandwidth: test actual contrast, grayscale settling, geometry and corner focus. 56 Hz/35 kHz is a fallback engineering option, not a silently substituted retail specification.
specification.oem: Ball HD-series HD17H, 17-inch horizontal-format OEM assembly, analog/linear-video option
specification.signal_path: Logix digital pixel index -> AION palette/controller -> 4-bit intensity DAC -> level-matched Ball analog input and linear amplifier. TTL/ECL-only input is not sufficient.
specification.rgb_palette_mapping: Preserve the 12-bit RGB command format. For grayscale, equal-channel values 000,111,...,FFF map to the corresponding 16 intensity codes. Other RGB values use a documented fixed luminance mapping, with DAC/gamma calibration qualified on the actual CRT.

change.title: Add composition history: Artemis 32 KiB prototype module
change.reason: Move the existing technical definition into a single composition-history version and retain the existing record-level requirements. Preserve the original DRAM type, chip count, capacity and physical layout and recorded 16-bit width. Add the known DRAM population plus separately identified PCB, connector contacts and passive-component sets. These six support-part definitions across the two RAM proposals are proposed engineering items, not claims of qualified suppliers or known electrical details. Each set is one defined supplied item; internal parts and any additional active circuitry still require engineering definition. Keep the first-use boundary unknown because no dated foundation reference was found, and use the simulation horizon for the final end. Do not backdate the module to the professional handover or promote it into a current commercial offering.
